summary: The study investigates the effects of surface chemistry on the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Ta3N5 barrier layers on low-k dielectrics such as organosilicates (OSG) and SiLK™. The process involves the use of TaCl5 and NH3 precursors, with nitrogen and hydrogen radical beams used for surface modification. The results show that nitrogen radicals significantly enhance chemisorption on OSG surfaces, leading to improved barrier formation and deposition rates. The study also highlights the importance of surface chemistry in ALD nucleation and growth behavior.
evidence: The initial chemisorption was found to be through formation of Ta–O bonding on organosilicates (OSG) and charge transfer complexes on aromatic SiLK™. The role of the atomic hydrogen in this process enhancement is discussed. The metal halide ALD process, TaCl5 + NH3 → Ta(N) + HCl, was chosen for its chemical simplicity. Samples were resistively heated to 300–390 °C by a molybdenum heating wire underneath the holding plate.
